subject.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)

question: Should OpenClaw preserve the existing effective same-session ContextEngine maintenance serialization, or intentionally adopt a public re-entrant maintain() contract for installed engines when this opt-in timeout fires?
rationale: This is a public plugin compatibility decision: host-side fencing cannot control engine-owned state, and a mechanical timeout change cannot establish that all existing engines tolerate overlap.

options.title: Preserve core-owned serialization
options.body: Release the interactive turn path while retaining or coalescing the plugin invocation tail so no same-session maintain calls overlap.

options.title: Adopt re-entrant engine semantics
options.body: Accept the new public contract only with explicit owner approval, migration guidance, and compatibility proof for installed context engines.

recommendation.title: Preserve core-owned serialization
recommendation.body: Release the interactive turn path while retaining or coalescing the plugin invocation tail so no same-session maintain calls overlap.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is a public ContextEngine contract and product compatibility decision rather than a narrow contributor implementation detail.
